purpose: Anchored 0-3 scoring of candidate datasets against one data requirement in data/requirements.csv. Score against the requirement, not against the dataset's general reputation.
scoring_rules: Score each criterion separately; do not let a high score on one criterion raise another.
Pick the highest level whose description is fully met. If unsure between two levels, take the lower and say why in score_rationale.
score_rationale cites the anchor for every criterion, e.g. 'fit=2: all MUST variables, office only (requirement: office+retail)'.
Unverified metadata (not checked in the dataset documentation or files) cannot support a level above 1 for quality, access, or reproducibility.
A candidate scored for several requirements needs a separate row per requirement when the scores differ.

score_fit.question: Does the dataset contain the MUST variables in the required context (building type, system, climate, occupancy)?

levels.0: A MUST variable is absent, or the context is different in a way that changes the phenomenon (e.g. residential data for a commercial HVAC RQ).
levels.1: Only some MUST variables, or the context differs enough that use requires a proxy argument.
levels.2: All MUST variables present; part of the context differs (e.g. one climate zone of the two required).
levels.3: All MUST variables present in the full required context.

score_coverage.question: Does the data span the minimum coverage in the requirement (period, seasons, number of buildings/zones/devices)?

levels.1: 50% to below 100% of the minimum coverage, or a required season/condition missing.
levels.3: Exceeds it enough to allow held-out, sensitivity, or transfer analysis (e.g. an extra year, building, or climate).

score_resolution.question: Do temporal and spatial resolution match the requirement?

levels.0: Coarser than required and the analysis cannot be done (e.g. monthly bills for an hourly forecasting RQ).
levels.1: Coarser than required; a changed aggregation or method could partly answer the RQ.
levels.3: Finer than required, allowing an aggregation sensitivity check.

score_quality.question: Are provenance and measurement quality documented?

levels.0: Origin, measurement method, or units unknown.
levels.1: Origin known, but sensors, calibration, timezone, or missing-data handling undocumented.
levels.2: Units, timezone, measurement points/equipment mapping, and missing-data handling documented.
levels.3: Level 2 plus documented calibration or QC procedure, and a peer-reviewed data paper or use in several independent studies.

score_access.question: Can the project legally obtain and use the data for this research?

levels.0: Not obtainable, or the license forbids this research use.
levels.1: Needs an application, contract, payment, or access only a human can perform.
levels.2: Obtainable after registration, or usable but not redistributable.
levels.3: Open license (e.g. CC-BY, CC0, ODbL) with direct download or API access.

score_cost.question: How much time, money, and preprocessing does use require? Higher is cheaper.

levels.0: Not feasible within the project's time or budget.
levels.1: Major cost: new measurement campaign, purchase, or extensive cleaning/semantic mapping.
levels.2: Moderate preprocessing (format conversion, alignment, point mapping).
levels.3: Usable as is or with minor preprocessing.

score_reproducibility.question: Can a third party obtain exactly the same data later?

levels.0: No fixed version; the same data cannot be obtained again (e.g. live dashboard only).
levels.1: Obtainable, but without version or persistent identifier.
levels.3: DOI for a fixed version, and acquisition can be scripted (code/data/acquire.py fetch).

decision_rules.satisfied_requires: A requirement is SATISFIED only by a SELECTED candidate with score_fit, score_coverage, and score_resolution all >= 2; otherwise the requirement is PARTIAL or PROXY with notes.
decision_rules.must_requirement_verification: A SELECTED candidate for a MUST requirement is re-scored by a second role (verified_by_role) that did not do the first scoring.
decision_rules.backup: Keep the best non-selected viable candidate as BACKUP so a later access or quality failure has a recorded alternative.
decision_rules.rubric_change: Changing anchors creates a new rubric_version; candidates scored with an older version are re-scored.
